what: Encode of the decoded twitter.cbor through ref_binding with sharedrefs::on, microseconds per document. v4: as in the run before (the write pass looks only at identities seen more than once; seen.reserve(1 << 17); seen on a std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource). v4b: v4 without the reserve. v5: v4, and the count pass returns after the identity of a value is counted when the value is neither an array, a map nor a registered tag, so it encodes no text, bytes or number into the discarding writer.
why: The owner asked to make encode with shared references much faster. Strings are shared by identity only, through tags 28 and 29; v5 still counts the identity of a string.
how: Google Benchmark, one binary per arm, each built twice (a, b). 3 rounds alternating, --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --benchmark_repetitions=3, random interleaving, GLIBC_TUNABLES trim_threshold, mmap_threshold and top_pad high.
finding: v4 1240/1219, v4b 1351/1375 (the reserve is worth 10 percent), v5 1127/1097 (-10 percent against v4). From the present library (about 1750) to v5: -37 percent; off is about 264.
